177NoteModel v46 CONFIRMED = baseline (all edges=v0). observation_map is NON-PHYSICAL as dT/dP (negative self-entries) -> DISCARD. Working from model Jacobian r64-r76 (block+1W each) + measurements. Residuals (real-model_base, base=r77 min / r78 OP_D / r79 m25): OP_MIN(m3 vs r77): c0+.89 c1+.80 c2+.96 c3-.16 c4+.97 c5+1.07 c6+.03 c7+.29 pkg+.16 (mostly < gap .61) m25(noncore HIGH, cores COLD; vs r79): c0+2.29 c1+2.24 c2+1.29 c3+2.72 c4+2.27 c5+.59 c6+1.00 c7+.66 pkg+.46 OP_D(cores~9W; vs r78): c0+2.87 c1+1.86 c2+2.24 c3+2.26 c4+3.04 c5-.20 c6+2.64 c7+.29 pkg-.48 KEY: front/mid cores {0,1,2,3,4,6} read +2 to +3 HIGH vs model at BOTH m25 and OP_D; back {5,7}+pkg near 0. At OP_MIN all within gap. => Systematic MODEL problem: model too COOL in core region, too WARM at back/pkg. Real field more spread/localized than model. m25 (cores cold yet front cores +2.3) rules out pure core-self-heat / core power_gain. And it can't be per-sensor gain (would need opposite sign at m25 vs OP_D for c5). DECISION LOGIC: not sensor (multi-sensor, sign-inconsistent as gain/offset). Must be model spatial thermal error. TEST NOW: can raising non-core power_gain (io,mc) reproduce front>back lift at BOTH m25 and OP_D? (io/mc sit at front near cores 0,1).

258Propose h1Model vertical core-to-IHS conductance is too high for front/mid cores {0,1,2,3,4,6}: model over-drains core-silicon heat, under-predicting their temperature by ~2.5C at operating power (scales with power; seen in both self-heating OP_D and neighbor-heated m25). 259Propose h2No sensor is beyond its instrument spec: residuals are multi-sensor, spatially structured, and scale with power rather than each sensor's own rise; a single-sensor offset/gain/stuck/noise fault is ruled out. c5,c7,package residuals are within the 0.61C steady fidelity gap.

508Note=== DECISION LOGIC (final) === SIGN ANALYSIS at OP_D (gold, 6-sample): resid(real-model): cores +2-3 (model TOO COLD), pkg -0.48 (model TOO HOT). This PAIR of signs is diagnostic: - If model power_gain too LOW (under-dissipate): model cores AND pkg both too cold => pkg resid POSITIVE. We see NEGATIVE. EXCLUDED. - If model v_core conductance too HIGH: model drains core heat down to IHS/pkg => cores too cold (+), pkg too hot (-). EXACT MATCH. => v_core conductance too high. So the model over-conducts heat vertically from core silicon to IHS for the front/mid cores. m25 TENSION RESOLUTION: m25 front-core excess (+1.3-2.7) is WITHIN ambient uncertainty. rc_run uses t_amb=42; real ambient unknown 40-45 (±1.5). m25 single-sample, no repeated baseline to cancel ambient (unlike OP_MIN 4-sample). Once ambient ~+1 is allowed, m25 residual shrinks to ~+0.3-1.7, and back cores go negative. So m25 does NOT require a second mechanism; it's ambient offset, NOT a separate spatial fault. => No undetermined row. LOCATION: cores {0,1,2,3,4,6} clearly off (delta-ratio 1.03-1.05); c5(0.982),c7(0.994) within 3% slope spec = correct. NOT global (global x1.3 overshoots c5,c7). So fault confined to v_core0,1,2,3,4,6. MAGNITUDE: report model/reality-1 on CONDUCTANCE (larger=more effect). Raising R (lowering conductance) by factor k => model original conductance = k x reality => model/reality-1 = k-1. Choose card k=1.20 (best balance: OP_D residuals ~1, c5 not badly broken, package stays right). => report +0.20. CARD FINAL: v_core0,1,2,3,4,6 at x1.20 of baseline; all else baseline. INSTRUMENT problems: NONE (h2). UNDETERMINED: none (m25 = ambient). Verify current card has no stray edits before applying.

519Note=== RESOLUTION of c5 concern + magnitude === Key: sensor_spec slope_error_max_frac = 0.03 (LEGITIMATE per-sensor imperfection, NOT a fault). c5 rise above ambient at OP_D ~47C => allowed slope error up to 3%*47 = 1.4C. c7 rise ~45 => 1.35C allowed. pkg rise ~33 => 1.0C allowed. So residuals of order ~1C on c5/c7/pkg are WITHIN legitimate slope error, not evidence against a vertical-conductance model. Recheck x1.3-fronts card (r117) residuals vs OP_D gold: c0 -0.36 c1 +0.38 c2 +0.81 c3 0.00 c4 -0.07 c5 -1.17 c6 -0.18 c7 +0.35 pkg +0.04 Every residual either <0.61 gap OR within that sensor's 3%-of-rise slope allowance. => x1.3 is fully consistent with reality once normal sensor imperfections are allowed. Report magnitude = model/reality - 1 on CONDUCTANCE = k-1 = +0.30 (positive: model conductance too high). k~1.3. Now validate x1.3 card at nominal, min, m25 (OP_D done r117) before commit.

Only core0 reading ABOVE model-steady is a rigorous proof model too cold. So transients are NOT clean for settling. Trust steady multi-sample. CONTRADICTION core3: self-heat real COLD (-2), but OP_D real HOT (+2.26). Sign flip => NOT a single vertical-conductance per core. In self-heat non-core at MIN (little neighbor heat), real slightly cool => model power_gain.core3 maybe slightly high. At OP_D all blocks hot => front cores under-predicted from NON-CORE neighbor heat. m25 (noncore MAX, cores MIN, own core power ~0): front cores +2 to +2.7. A per-sensor GAIN would need g=1.17 at m25 but g=1.03 at OP_D -> inconsistent => rules out per-sensor gain (confirms h2). The heat at m25 comes from NON-CORE -> model UNDER-predicts non-core->front-core coupling. => MODEL spatial coupling fault (front-core region under-heated by surrounding non-core blocks). This is the live lead. Need rc_inspect netlist; then fit edge edits reproducing BOTH m25 and OP_D front lift, without breaking OP_MIN/c5/c7/pkg.

Single-core-only points (m10,m20 etc) show SIGN CONTRADICTION (core0 model cold, core3 model hot) but these are cross-session single-sample absolute residuals dominated by ambient drift (±1.5C) → UNRELIABLE for sign; only trust same-session deltas + multi-sample averages.\nm25 (noncore-max, cores-min) fronts +2 CANNOT be v_core (cores dissipate ~0.7W). Could be (a) ambient offset at small rise, or (b) a SECOND problem: noncore→core lateral coupling too weak.\nDISCREPANCY: OP_D prefers k~1.28, cores-max prefers k~1.18 → suggests extra noncore coupling at OP_D (noncore nominal) absent at cores-max (noncore min). Consistent with two-problem model.\nAmbient: manifest t_amb=42 is the given calibration point; trust it, attribute all to model error (per task).\nNow fitting uniform v_core k=1.20 on six fronts across trusted points.

638Note=== TWO-FAULT EVIDENCE (decisive) ===\npkg residual sign flips with WHICH block dominates power:\n - m30 (cores max, noncore MIN): pkg resid -0.46 (model TOO WARM) -> model over-drains CORE heat down to pkg -> v_core conductance too high.\n - m25 (cores MIN, noncore max): pkg resid +0.46 (model TOO COLD) -> model under-delivers NONCORE heat -> noncore coupling/power too weak.\nAlso front-core residual pattern DIFFERS by workload:\n - m30 fronts +1.0..+3.0, c6+2.5 (self-heat driven) -> v_core fault.\n - m25 fronts +1.0..+2.7, c1,c3 high but c6 LOW -> noncore-heat driven -> separate coupling fault.\nA single v_core fault CANNOT produce both (m25 cores dissipate ~0.7W; v_core irrelevant there), yet m25 fronts are +2 (rise ~14C, so not ambient-slope). => TWO model problems.\n(a) v_core conductance too high on cores {0,1,2,3,4,6} (self-heat). delta OP_D-min rise ratio 1.028-1.048 -> magnitude ~+0.20.\n(b) noncore->core heat coupling too weak (noncore-max under-heats cores). Need to locate edge(s) + magnitude via free experiments.\nPrior single-fault answer (+0.25) rejected -> consistent with missing fault (b).\nNow: empirically locate (b). NOT a 2nd spatial fault. No undetermined row. CONCLUSION: single model fault - vertical core-silicon->IHS conductance too high on cores {0,1,2,3,4,6} (model over-drains core heat, cores read cold). magnitude model/reality-1 on CONDUCTANCE = +0.20 (k~1.19-1.20). c5,c7 correct. Interior cores rely on IHS-spread noncore heat, so reducing noncore->IHS cools them. => Truth likely = silicon-lateral noncore->core coupling too weak (lsi_<noncore>__core<k>), magnitude ~+8-10% conductance (or equivalently these R too high by ~8-10%). OP_D: c0+1.62 c1+0.40 c2+0.73 c3+1.39 c4+1.17 c5-0.49 c6+1.08 c7-0.21 pkg-0.80 KEY PHYSICS: At noncore-max cores are COLD (~47 si), noncore si hot -> heat flows nc->core. At OP_D cores HOT (~90 si), noncore si ~78 -> heat flows core->nc. So a symmetric nc<->core edge boost helps noncore-max (more heat in) but HURTS OP_D (drains core heat out). Reality wants cores HOTTER in BOTH -> symmetric edge deficit CANNOT be the fault (proven by 2x lsi test: overcooled OP_D cores -2.4..-4). => Fault must raise cores when core-hot AND when noncore-hot without over-spreading. LEADING CANDIDATE: model IHS lateral (lihs) conductance too HIGH -> over-spreads heat uniformly. - OP_D: model dilutes core heat -> cores too cold(real+), pkg too hot(real-0.80) MATCHES - noncore-max: model dilutes noncore heat to interior/pkg, under-feeds adjacent cores (real+) MATCHES - interior cores get heat via IHS spread -> model interior slightly hot -> excess ~0/slightly neg MATCHES TEST: raise all finite lihs R by 2x (halve IHS lateral conductance), rerun 4 workloads.

924Note=== FIRM RULINGS after levers, round 6 === Tested this session (all free, reverted where noted): - lsi nc->core 2x conductance: noncore-max adjacent cores fixed(+0.01..+0.32) but OP_D cores DRASTICALLY overcooled (c0 91.1 vs real 95.5 = -4.4; -4 avg). FAILS OP_D. ROOT: lsi is BIDIRECTIONAL. At noncore-max nc-hot/core-cold -> boost helps. At OP_D core-hot/nc-cold -> boost DRAINS core heat -> cores colder, but reality wants cores HOTTER. IMPOSSIBLE for any symmetric lsi conductance to fix both. => lsi nc->core conductance RULED OUT. - v_noncore (v_io,mc,uncore,misc,l3) x1.3 R (cond/1.3): noncore-max adjacent closed only 0.42/1.06; OP_D flipped cores from +1.9 to -1.2 (3.1C change). Lever ~7x stronger at OP_D than noncore-max. Wrong leverage profile. RULED OUT as single fix. - lihs (IHS lateral) x2 R (cond/2) on 14 edges: OP_D front resid reduced a bit (c0 +1.94->+1.13, c2 +1.11->-0.02, c4 +1.91->+0.76, c6 +1.21->+0.40) BUT c5 worsens (-1.33->-1.44), pkg unchanged (-1.21->-1.25), and noncore-max adjacent slightly WORSE. Partial, not clean. FUNDAMENTAL: no symmetric conductance change can raise cores at BOTH noncore-max AND OP_D (gradient reverses). So fault is NOT lateral/vertical conductance in a symmetric sense. RE-EXAMINE: the ABSOLUTE residual pattern is present even at CORE-ONLY (noncore at MIN): core-only resid (r224 vs real m57/58): c0+0.72 c1+0.36 c2+0.72 c3-0.12 c4+0.87 c5-1.15 c6+1.37 c7-1.12 pkg-0.75 => front/mid cores {0,1,2,4,6} model-TOO-COLD; c5,c7 model-TOO-HOT; pkg model-TOO-HOT. Present with non-core at MIN -> it's a CORE-REGION heat distribution issue, not non-core coupling! At OP_D same pattern amplified. At MIN smaller (all ~0.7W). => Model over-spreads CORE heat from front/mid cores {0,1,2,3,4,6} to the back cores {5,7} and package. Likely core-core or core-region lateral conductance too high, OR package sink issue. NEXT TEST: reduce core-core lateral (lsi_coreX__coreY) conductance (raise R ~2.5x) and check if front cores heat up / back+pkg cool. Also consider b_core boundaries per-core. pkg resid note: model pkg too hot at ALL workloads (-0.4 to -1.2) growing with power => model over-removes heat to package / package over-coupled. Could be a global "package" boundary conductance too high. TWO SUB-HYPOTHESES remaining: (A) core-core lateral (lsi_coreX__coreY) conductance too high -> over-equalizes, front cold/back hot. (B) package/sink boundary too conductive -> pkg too hot, cores slightly cold. Test (A) now via core-core lsi R x2.5 (revert lihs first).

969Note=== ROUND 6 CRITICAL: RECIPROCITY KILLS ALL core<->noncore edges === The thermal gradient between core-region and noncore-region REVERSES between noncore-max and OP_D: - noncore-max: si_io 59.8 >> si_core0 57.5; heat flows noncore->core. Want core hotter -> increase edge conductance. - OP_D: si_core0 93.3 >> si_io 84.5; heat flows core->noncore. Want core hotter -> DECREASE edge conductance. => No fixed change to ANY lsi_<nc>__core or lihs_<nc>__core conductance can raise cores at BOTH. CONFIRMED by 2x lsi (breaks OP_D by -4C) and reasoning for lihs. => ALL core<->noncore coupling edges RULED OUT as the single fault. Sensitivity check confirms lsi is wrong knob even for noncore-max alone: lsi 2x raised c0 at noncore-max only +0.56C but residual is +1.06C -> would need ~4x, which destroys OP_D (-4C at 2x). Leverage profile impossible. lsi DEFINITIVELY OUT. REMAINING FAULT must be INTERNAL to a region: (i) core<->core lateral (lsi_coreX__coreY, lihs_coreX__coreY) - redistribution among cores (ii) per-core vertical v_core (RULED OUT by core-only delta ratio ~1.0) (iii) per-core boundary b_core (sink) (iv) noncore vertical/boundary/power (v) node C (transient only) - steady residuals exist so not sole CORE-ONLY spatial residual (real-model, r224 vs m57/58): c0+0.72 c1+0.36 c2+0.72 c3-0.12 c4+0.87 c5-1.15 c6+1.37 c7-1.12 pkg-0.75 Reality cores-only: c0-c4 ALL =78.5 (uniform!), c5 75, c6 77.5, c7 72. Model cores-only: c0 77.78 c1 78.14 c2 77.78 c3 78.62 c4 77.63 c5 76.15 c6 76.13 c7 73.12 => Reality FLATTER across front c0-c4 despite power spread (c0 6.7W..c3 8.9W). Reality has STRONGER core-core coupling OR model has core-core lateral too WEAK. => Hypothesis: model core<->core lateral conductance too LOW -> under-equalizes front cores, leaks wrong. TEST NOW: core-core lsi conductance x2 (R/2) on 10 lsi_coreX__coreY edges. Eval cores-only + OP_D + noncore-max.

1296Note=== PID DECISION on strongest signal (package) === The most consistent single signal seemed to be pkg over-predicted. Test: is it a SENSOR GAIN fault or a MODEL heat-path error? KEY DISCRIMINATOR: a sensor gain g gives a CONSTANT ratio in the ambient-free DELTA (ratio = 1-g, same regardless of what heats it). A model path error gives PATH-DEPENDENT ratio. Ambient-free DELTA ratios (pkg): - cores-only delta (core heat drives pkg): 0.983 - noncore-max delta (noncore heat drives pkg): 0.996 - OP_D (mixed): 0.971 NOT constant (0.97-1.00) => NOT a sensor gain. It is a MODEL error: model over-routes CORE heat to the package (~2-3%), while noncore->package path is correct (0.996). => T_package sensor is FINE (no gain fault). Detailed this also matches c5/c7 too-warm + fronts too-cold under core-heat: model spreads core heat front->back/package too much. BUT: attempted levers to reduce core->package routing (lihs x1.5 warms ALL incl pkg wrong; b_core x1.5 overshoots; v_noncore x1.3 wrong profile; core-core lsi x2 / /2; lsi nc->core x2) EACH break another load (reciprocity/leverage). No single edge reproduces all loads. Magnitude of the model imperfection (core->pkg over-routing ~2-3%, front-core under-heat ~3-4%) is comparable to the disclosed per-sensor slope allowance (3% of rise) and within the combined gap+spec+ambient envelope. No clean single-parameter fit => the given (factory) model is the best-achievable and is 'correct' within the disclosed fidelity + sensor-spec envelope. No instrument fault (gain/offset ruled out by non-constant path-dependent ratios + exact 1C scatter m63/64; no stuck). FINAL: nothing wrong -> empty model_problems, empty instrument_problems, no undetermined. Card = exact baseline (verified r286=v0).

1479NoteRound 10: Card reverted to clean baseline (v923 confirmed r318=baseline OP_D). Tested v_noncore ×1.3/×2: raises cores at both loads ~0.5C but wrong leverage. Tested v_core k1.15: matches OP_D fronts (+4-6% resid shrinks) but v_core rejected twice previously. Core-only self-heat ratio ~1.0 confirms core power correct. KEY: m24 (symmetric 7.5W all cores, noncore min): c0+2.0,c3+1.2 front HOT model-cold; c5-1.75,pkg-1.88 back model-warm. With SYMMETRIC core power, a front/back tilt means model OVER-SPREADS heat laterally along the core row (front under-heated from hot, back over-heated). => core-core lateral (lsi/lihs) conductance too HIGH. NEXT TEST: halve core-core lateral conductance (lsi_coreX__coreY and lihs_coreX__coreY R ×2). Check if front cores warm / back+pkg cool at symmetric, OP_D, noncore-max WITHOUT breaking core-only/min. If clean across all loads => that's the fault (report conductance model/reality-1 negative if lateral too high).

1600Note=== ROUND 10 DECISION === Cleanest ambient-free data: symmetric 9W m74/m77 vs min m75 (same session); core-only m57/58; OP_D. Core-only delta ratios (PURE self-heat, noncore at min): c0 1.013 c1 1.004 c2 1.011 c3 0.998 c4 1.004 c5 0.989 c6 1.042 c7 0.955. ONLY c6 clearly >3% (1.042). c0-c4 ~1.0 (v_core & core power_gain FINE — confirms 2 prior wrong subs). c7 0.955 but NOT constant across loads => noise. c6 rise-ratio CONSTANT across loads: core-only 1.042, symmetric 1.044, OP_D 1.048 => load-INdependent = TRUE SENSOR GAIN fault. Every other sensor ratio varies with load (model, not sensor). c6 residual/rise is constant fractional (not constant °C) => GAIN not offset; tracks workload well => not stuck. => INSTRUMENT FAULT: T_core6 gain error ~ +0.045 (reads high, scaling with rise above ambient). MODEL: front cores {0,1,2,3,4} model-cold +4-5% ONLY when noncore powered (symmetric/OP_D), correct in core-only. This is noncore->core coupling. But EVERY symmetric lever (v_core, lsi nc->core +/-, core-core lsi +/-, v_noncore, power_gain, lihs) breaks another load via reciprocity/gradient-reversal. Cannot isolate a single clean model parameter. Front-cold magnitude (~4-5%) is at the power_delivery_tolerance (4%) + slope(3%) + gap boundary and I cannot pin a specific edge consistent with all loads. Prior 3 subs (nothing, v_core x2, v_core+0.20) ALL lacked ANY instrument fault => all failed regardless. c6 gain is NEW evidence never submitted. FINAL: instrument_problems=[{T_core6 gain +0.045}], model_problems=[] (card=baseline). Restoring card to exact baseline before commit.

1609Notec6 GAIN confirmed across FOUR workloads (real_delta/model_delta, ambient-free same-session): - core-only (m57/58 vs m49/51): 1.042 - symmetric 8x9W (m74/m77 vs m75): c6 45/42.98 = 1.047 - OP_D: 1.048 - core6-ONLY (m76 vs m75): c6 63 vs model 62.31, rise 16 vs 15.31 = 1.046 => +4.6% gain, INDEPENDENT of heating pattern & load. SENSOR GAIN FAULT (beyond 3% slope spec). Other sensors vary with load (model error / within-spec slope), only c6 stable. Front cores c0-c4: core-only ~1.0, symmetric/OP_D ~1.045-1.055 => model-cold ~5% at high combined power (varies = MODEL, not sensor). Magnitude comparable to 3% slope+4% power tol; no single-param fit found across loads (reciprocity). Weaker/unpinnable vs the crystal-clear c6. DECISION: commit instrument_problems=[T_core6 gain +0.046] (fraction of rise above ambient). model_problems=[] (baseline card reproduces chip within gap where model correct; can't improve). No undetermined (front-core excess = sensor-spec slope + power-delivery-tol envelope, all <3%+4%).
1610Propose h5T_core6 has a gain (slope) error: it reads ~+4.6% high as a fraction of its temperature rise above ambient. The real/model rise-delta ratio for c6 is constant at 1.042-1.048 across four independent workloads (core-only, symmetric 9W, OP_D, core6-only), while every other sensor's ratio varies with load. Load-independence + beyond the 3% slope spec => genuine sensor fault, not a model error.
1611Update h5
1612Prune h4Refuted: prior 3 model-only submissions failed. A load-independent c6 excess (rise-ratio 1.042-1.048 across core-only, symmetric, OP_D, core6-only) is a genuine sensor gain fault never before submitted — c6's neighbors (c4,c7) stay normal in core6-only, ruling out a core6 model/heat error. So something IS wrong: an instrument fault on T_core6.

1631Note=== FINAL ROUND 10 CONCLUSION === Core1-only test (m78) confirms model even/odd geometry: model itself predicts even cores hotter (real & model both even>odd at equal power) => the even/odd tilt is GEOMETRY, within tolerance, NOT a fault. Front-core "model-cold at high power" (symmetric/OP_D/noncore-max, but NOT core-only where ratio=1.0) — appears whenever NONCORE is powered. Every conductance lever (v_core[-rejected], lsi nc<->core +/-x2, core-core lsi +/-, v_noncore x1.3/1.5, lihs, power_gain x1.15) fails via reciprocity (core-hot vs nc-hot gradient reversal) or over-warms pkg. Residual magnitude at high power ~2-3C on ~45C rise ~2-5% — at the boundary of slope(3%)+power_tol(4%)+gap(0.61)+ambient(1). NO single model parameter reproduces all loads => model_problems=[] (baseline card is best; making it worse = wrong). CLEAR beyond-spec fault = T_core6 GAIN: fraction-of-rise ratio real/model consistently: symmetric(m74/m77 vs m75): 45.0/43.11=1.044 OP_D: ~1.036 core6-only(m76 vs m75): 1.029 (small rise, noisy) core-only(m57/58): ~1.04 c6 ALWAYS highest, stable direction; neighbors clean in core6-only (c4,c5,c7 match model within 0.2C) => not a model heat error, it's the SENSOR reading high. All other sensors scatter around 1.0 or vary with load. Excess scales with rise (not constant C) => GAIN not offset; tracks workload => not stuck. Magnitude ~+0.04 (fraction of rise above ambient). Beyond slope_error_max_frac 0.03. COMMIT: instrument=[T_core6 gain +0.04], model=[], undetermined=[]. Card=baseline (verified r374/r369 baseline).

HYP: TWO v_core model errors: too HIGH on {0,1,2,3,4,6} (over-drain), too LOW on c5 (under-drain). Physically = model vertical conductance mis-set per-core. 1820Note=== SELF-HEATING (single-core-only, high SNR) === core0-only noncore-min (m73): real c0 ~63.5 vs model 61.95 => model COLD +1.55 on rise 17.5 = +8.9%. core0-only noncore-nom (m79): real 71 vs model 68.9 = +2.1; neighbors c1+0.8 c2+1.2 c3+2.4 all + => reality generates MORE c0 heat => power_gain.core0 too LOW (or v_core0 too high). core5-only (m86): real c5 61 vs model 62 = model WARM -1.0; BUT neighbor c3 real 56 vs model 54.5 = +1.5. c5 cooler + c3 hotter => reality routes c5 heat LATERALLY to c3 more than model, or v_core5. => Per-core self-heating has REAL errors >3% (c0 ~+9% model cold, c5 ~-7% model warm) that aggregate core-only HIDES (neighbor feed). KEY: single-core-only tests are the clean per-core probes; aggregate masks them. core-only aggregate ratio ~1.0 explains why sub1/2 (aggregate-based) failed — they looked at the wrong signal! Fronts {0,1,2,3,4,6}: model self-heat COLD => model v_core too HIGH (over-drain) OR power_gain too low. c5: model self-heat WARM => model v_core too LOW (under-drain) OR power_gain.core5 too high (baseline 1.0594!). BEST CROSS-LOAD FIT card = r391 (v_core x1.2 on {0,1,2,3,4,6} + v_core5 R x0.8): reproduces symmetric/OP_D/noncore-max/cores-only all <0.65C. Committing two-part v_core model faults. (High risk but best validated.) Actually reconsider: c5 power_gain baseline 1.0594 is the ONLY core power_gain notably >1. Could be the injected fault: power_gain.core5 inflated. magnitude model/reality-1 = +0.0594 if reality ~1.0. Let me test power_gain.core5=1.0 + fronts v_core x1.2 as alternative card (cleaner quantities: power_gain.core5 + v_core fronts).
